description: GLM-5.3-Flash on one DGX Spark with KindlingAI's gr8, a from-scratch CUDA inference engine (no vLLM, PyTorch or NCCL at serve time). The weights are KindlingAI's exlr8 release at its bit201 manifest (K2, with the 124 routed experts that carry the most routing weight at tool-call positions at K3, about 2.01 bits a routed weight), int4 KV, DFlash2 speculative decoding for a request alone, four requests at once (SESS=4) sharing a 700,032-token KV pool, one prefill lane, and a prompt cache on disk. Text only. The recipe runs the creator's published image of commit ad0c7148 (kindlingai/glm-5.3-flash-exlr8-1x-spark, gr8 d598965) with a placement wrapper that uses the release in place from the read-only model mounts, the DFlash2 drafter converted on its first start. Options: speed or long context (one request up to 700,018 tokens); the bit201 or k2 manifest; DFlash2 or MTP only. Creator claims, unmeasured here: 53.8 tok/s for one request writing code, 995 tok/s prefill at 8K, 43.5 / 41.3 / 53.4 / 57.5 tok/s aggregate at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 streams; the weights take about 93 GB of memory (bit201 about 0.4 GB more than k2) and the boot keeps 5 GiB free. The creator's notes: the low bitrate encourages loops, so test long agentic runs after any update. Thinking is always on in GLM 5.3's template: a request that turns it off gets HTTP 400 (the creator's default), and a small max_tokens can end inside the thinking. The mounted width files are read whole (about 196 GB), where the creator's launcher range-fetches about 87 GB from Hugging Face. Licences, for information: the weights and engine are MIT (Z.AI's notice kept); the DFlash2 drafter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial).
title: GLM 5.3 Flash EXLR8 gr8 one Spark
